THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for secret detection. Read by the TypeScript
classifier (packages/core/src/gate/patterns.ts), the PowerShell scanner
(automation/scripts/governance/Invoke-SecretScan.ps1), the pre-commit hook
(.githooks/pre-commit) and the leak scan (scripts/leak-scan.mjs).
D5: `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` cannot match `sk-proj-` or `sk-ant-` — the hyphen
ends the character run after three characters. The flagship OpenAI and
Anthropic shapes were therefore structurally unmatchable, and tests written
from the same mental model passed. Every rule below ships with a `fixture`
it MUST match and the file ships `benign` strings no rule may match. Both
are asserted in CI (gate/key-shapes).
D24 / I17 — BANDING. `band: definite` may fail a commit. `band: heuristic`
may raise a tier, annotate, or warn, and may NEVER fail a commit. A fuzzy
rule blocking a commit is how a hook earns a `--no-verify` habit, and a
guard that is routed around is worse than no guard because it also carries
the belief that it is protecting you.
I15 — this file is CONTENT-HASHED. Changing it invalidates the last full
corpus scan and blocks a release until `sutra rescan` completes. A better
list changes nothing retroactively; ship the re-scan trigger, not just a
longer list.
Adding a provider to automation/policies/provider-router.json without adding
its key shape here is a bug. CI asserts the two stay in step.

rules.description: Legacy OpenAI key. Requires 32+ chars with no hyphen, which is what keeps `sk-learning-and-development-notes` out.
GitHub classic PAT / OAuth / user / server / refresh token
JSON Web Token with a payload — an OAuth access/refresh token shape
SAP BTP / Datasphere OAuth client id-secret shape

A key=value shape. CANNOT distinguish `password=dbutler_prod_9x2Kq` (a real secret) from `password=db_password` (a variable reference) — they are structurally identical, so no regex separates them. Therefore HEURISTIC: it floors the tier, it never blocks a commit. An attempt to tighten this was written and reverted: the tightened version stopped flooring an identifier-shaped literal password, trading a harmless false positive for a harmful false negative.
An Authorization: Bearer header carrying a live token. Heuristic because documentation legitimately shows the shape.
A database URI carrying an inline password

$floor_paths_comment: D4: these were matched with StartsWith against a PARA-NUMBERED vault
(`11-identity/...`), so no real path could ever match and one of the three
secret-floor layers had never once fired. It is present, plausible, and
documented — and a rule that fires zero times looks exactly like a rule
The matcher is therefore SEGMENT-BASED and number-prefix-insensitive:
Rule-hit counts are recorded so a permanently-cold rule is visible in
$ocr_comment: I16 / D14: every one of the worst credential cases in the source system
entered as an IMAGE OF TEXT — a PDF or OneNote export run through Tesseract
— i.e. exactly where no human ever reads the result. An extract produced by
one of these engines is floored to `local_only` regardless of how benign its
text looks, and is never eligible for a hosted route on an ingest-time tier
